messages.content: You are an accelerator evaluating the target company, not its founder. Write in third person; never say our product, our fees, we charge or our business model. reason_to_meet explains why the accelerator should spend time on this company. Write a short company brief for an accelerator deciding whether to meet the founders. Explain the product and its buyer in everyday language. Describe what gets delivered and who pays, not just the advertised technology. reason_to_meet is the business opportunity, explicitly a hypothesis where unproven. main_risk must explain a mechanism by which the company could fail to earn money: delivery/service costs exceeding fees, cash paid before collection, weak repeat demand, or another relevant driver. Choose the actual driver indicated by this business; do not merely question AI accuracy or say the technology is unproven. first_question must name ONE concrete operating record to inspect (a ledger, invoice, cohort/retention report, signed contract, cost breakdown, cash-flow statement, or similar) that would test the main risk. Never phrase it as "Has X grown/demonstrated/shown..." -- that asks for a claimed outcome, not a record. Bad: "Has the company shown consistent revenue growth?" Good: "Can you share the monthly revenue ledger for the past six months?" Do not merely repeat that financial data is missing.

{"company_name": "Synthetic example: machinery maintenance service", "evidence": [{"id": "C1", "passage": "We maintain packaging machinery for food processors. Our founder previously managed a large maintenance department."}]}

{"business": "The company describes a maintenance service for food processors' packaging equipment.", "reason_to_meet": "Recurring maintenance needs could support repeat contracts if servicing costs leave a margin.", "main_risk": "Travel, replacement parts and unplanned callouts could consume the maintenance fee; the founder's prior role does not establish this company's economics.", "first_question": "Can you share completed work orders with billed fees, parts costs and technician hours?", "evidence_ids": ["C1"]}

{"company_name": "Synthetic example: parts exchange", "evidence": [{"id": "C1", "passage": "We match spare-part buyers with distributors and collect a commission on orders."}]}

{"business": "The company describes matching spare-part buyers with distributors and earning order commissions.", "reason_to_meet": "Repeat parts purchases could support a useful exchange if commissions cover the work needed to complete orders.", "main_risk": "Exception handling, refunds and payment costs could consume commission revenue; the value of parts traded is not the company's revenue.", "first_question": "Can you share the order ledger separating order value, commission, refunds and fulfillment costs?", "evidence_ids": ["C1"]}

Write an introductory email from an accelerator to the TARGET COMPANY founders, offering useful work. We are not the target company or its customer. Address the explicit founder request when supplied. State what the company does in observation, then propose a specific deliverable our research/drafting tools can produce in proposed_help. The subject names that deliverable. meeting_ask is a short question inviting a conversation about the proposed work. Do not copy the research question into the invitation. Do not promise funding, introductions, customer access, results or work already completed. Do not sell the founders their own product. Use natural, concise email language, not generic partnership or promotional copy.
{"company_name": "Synthetic example: ceramic exporter", "evidence": [{"id": "C1", "passage": "We export ceramic tableware and are looking for help identifying overseas restaurant distributors."}]}

{"subject": "A distributor research brief for your ceramic exports", "observation": "I saw that you are looking for restaurant distributors for your ceramic tableware.", "proposed_help": "We could prepare a sourced distributor shortlist with product fit and unanswered qualification questions. We could also draft an introduction tailored to each distributor for you to review.", "meeting_ask": "Would you be open to a call about which markets and distributor requirements to prioritize?", "evidence_ids": ["C1"]}

Choose ONE TO THREE distinct priorities that most reduce uncertainty about THIS company or address its actual founder request. You decide the work, order, deliverables and completion criteria from the evidence. There is no fixed demand/economics/deck sequence. A pre-revenue laboratory, hotel operator and profitable manufacturer need different work. Explain why_now and required_input for every action. Build on existing records and calculated figures instead of requesting them again. If a record is missing, name exactly what is needed and why; do not manufacture it. Each action must produce a usable artifact and test a specific investor question. If one action needs an earlier output, state that dependency. A website claim is not proof of growth. Customer savings are not company profitability. Where relevant, distinguish recognized revenue, GMV, direct costs, overhead and cash timing. Complete when results are recorded honestly, including adverse outcomes. Do not invent numerical targets, forecasts, resources, access or dates. Proposed work is not completed work. Do not invent actions the available tools have executed.
{"company_name": "Synthetic example: water sensor prototype", "evidence": [{"id": "C1", "passage": "We have a laboratory water sensor prototype; field reliability has not been tested."}]}

{"priorities": [{"title": "Design the field-reliability evidence record", "why_now": "Laboratory performance does not establish reliability in the intended field environment.", "required_input": "Laboratory calibration reports and the intended field operating conditions.", "investor_question": "Can the sensor maintain useful accuracy outside laboratory conditions?", "action": "Draft a field-test protocol comparing sensor readings with a reference method, recording drift, failed readings and maintenance effort.", "output": "Field-test protocol and results-recording worksheet.", "done_when": "The protocol specifies the comparison, conditions and failure recording needed to decide whether redesign or a field pilot is justified."}], "evidence_ids": ["C1"]}

Write the preliminary investment case itself. Explain the observed customer problem and how this business creates value; distinguish monetization from customer value and label an unknown charging model as unknown. Address the explicit founder request where present. Explain the strongest evidence for spending effort, and the disconfirming evidence. Separate observed facts, hypotheses and unknowns. If suitability is unclear, write a screening decision memo that resolves the company-type/engagement ambiguity; do not fabricate an investable case.

{"company": "Synthetic example: cold-chain operator", "sources": [{"id": "E1", "quote": "We store produce in refrigerated warehouses and charge customers for occupied storage space. We arrange transport through contractors."}]}

{"title": "Cold-chain storage: test utilization and cash collection", "purpose": "Decide whether recurring storage demand can cover refrigeration and handling costs.", "decision_question": "Does paid storage utilization support positive delivery contribution?", "sections": [{"heading": "Reason to investigate", "content": "The company describes charging for occupied refrigerated storage and arranging contracted transport. Recurring produce storage could support repeat business, but the source does not establish occupancy, prices or payment collection."}, {"heading": "Objection and decisive test", "content": "Refrigeration and handling costs continue when occupied capacity falls. Match occupied storage days to invoices and collections, then deduct electricity, handling, transport obligations and spoilage claims. Report loss-making periods as well as profitable ones."}], "missing_inputs": [{"record": "Monthly occupied capacity, storage invoices, collections and direct site-cost ledger for the same warehouses and periods", "why": "These records distinguish billed utilization from collected revenue and show the cost of serving it."}], "next_action": "Prepare a warehouse-month reconciliation worksheet and request the corresponding occupancy, invoice and cost records.", "completion_test": "The worksheet reconciles comparable storage periods to revenue and delivery costs and explains missing records, unpaid balances and adverse contribution.", "evidence_ids": ["E1"]}

Produce a company-specific founder interview and commercial validation working document. Write the actual questions, proposed customer segment, test procedure, records to collect, comparison and stop/continue decision criteria. Choose a test suitable for this business and maturity. No invented targets, assumed customers or claim that a test was executed. If fit is unclear, focus on the questions that resolve it.
{"company": "Synthetic example: reusable produce crates", "sources": [{"id": "E1", "quote": "We rent reusable crates to wholesalers and collect the empties for reuse."}]}

{"title": "Reusable-crate pilot: test returns and collection cost", "purpose": "Prepare a bounded test of whether crate rental can cover losses, cleaning and return transport.", "decision_question": "Can rental receipts cover the complete crate-return cycle?", "sections": [{"heading": "Questions for the wholesale buyer", "content": "Who approves crate rental and pays for lost crates? Which produce route would you test? What packaging do you use today, and what do packaging disposal, damaged goods and empty-container storage cost? Ask for the corresponding route records rather than claimed savings."}, {"heading": "Pilot procedure and recording sheet", "content": "Propose one agreed wholesale route and compare it with its existing packaging process. Record issued crates, returned crates, damage, rental billed, payment collected, cleaning effort and collection charges for the same cycle. A proposed pilot is not evidence that a customer has agreed to it."}, {"heading": "Decision after the test", "content": "Compare rental receipts with the full return-cycle delivery costs and investigate missing crates and unpaid invoices. If costs exceed receipts, change price, collection design or scope before scaling. Buyer willingness to repeat must be recorded separately from operational savings."}], "missing_inputs": [{"record": "Current route packaging invoices and proposed crate-rental, loss and collection terms", "why": "They define a comparable baseline and who bears losses and transport costs."}], "next_action": "Draft the route pilot worksheet and ask the founder to confirm the proposed buyer, baseline and loss-allocation terms.", "completion_test": "The protocol defines a comparable route, measurement fields and an adverse-result decision before any claim of successful testing.", "evidence_ids": ["E1"]}

Write an initial investor narrative with concrete company-specific content: business, customer problem, evidence for demand/economics, risks and the milestone financing would support. Missing capital amount, runway, valuation or metrics remain explicitly unknown, with exact source requests. Do not invent investor names, financial projections or fundraising activity. This is an internal narrative draft, not a final CIM.

{"company": "Synthetic example: machine retrofit developer", "sources": [{"id": "E1", "quote": "We develop energy-efficiency retrofits for factory machines. Our prototype has been tested in our workshop; we want to evaluate it at a customer site."}]}

{"title": "Retrofit financing narrative and pilot budget questions", "purpose": "Explain the next proof milestone and the records needed before sizing external capital.", "decision_question": "What capital would fund a credible customer-site demonstration?", "sections": [{"heading": "Business and next proof point", "content": "The company describes an energy-efficiency retrofit tested in its own workshop. Its proposed next milestone is a customer-site evaluation. A financing argument would need to connect measured energy effects with installation, reliability and customer economics; none is established by the current source."}, {"heading": "Use of proceeds and open objections", "content": "A proposed budget should distinguish prototype revisions, installation, measurement equipment and evaluation labor from ongoing overhead. Ask who will host and pay for the test, who owns resulting IP, and what failure would trigger redesign. The raise amount, valuation and financing terms cannot yet be sized from the supplied evidence."}], "missing_inputs": [{"record": "Workshop test report, proposed site-test scope and itemized supplier and labor estimates", "why": "They connect the next proof milestone to a costed work package."}, {"record": "Dated available cash, existing obligations and ownership register", "why": "They show the funding gap and ownership context before proposing financing terms."}], "next_action": "Prepare a milestone budget worksheet listing site-test costs, existing resources and unresolved estimates.", "completion_test": "Every budget line has a dated source or an explicit missing estimate, and the narrative separates workshop observations from proposed site performance.", "evidence_ids": ["E1"]}
Assess whether initial company research and fundraising-preparation work is useful, not whether to invest capital. Cite company evidence and state the specific next deliverable.

{"company": "Synthetic example: factory heat controls", "observed_maturity": "early_business", "sources": [{"id": "E1", "quote": "We develop heat controls for factories and are seeking introductions to plant operators for pilot discussions."}]}

{"decision": "proceed", "rationale": "The early-stage company has asked for help reaching plant operators. A sourced prospect brief and a proposed pilot discussion outline would address that request. Initial preparation is useful without claiming the company is ready for investment or that we can guarantee introductions.", "next_action": "Prepare a researched plant-operator prospect brief and draft a founder proposal to confirm pilot scope.", "evidence_ids": ["E1"]}
